author: val
body: GopBuf and the drawing primitives on it were moved to UI chapter PixelBuf on 2026-07-28 so that any application could reach them, unchanged and under the same names, so no call site moved. What stays here is what is genuinely the shell's: the hardware framebuffer address, the three font roles and the wheel they load into, glyph blitting through those fonts, and the saved-pixels cursor.

author: val
body: Keeps its arity because it is the entry point applications draw free-standing text through, and free-standing text has no box: DiffusionApp and CalendarApp call it with bare coordinates. It is gop-buf-put-text-role-clip with the buffer width supplied, so there is ONE dispatch rather than two that can drift apart. Same shape for gop-buf-put-text over gop-buf-put-text-clip and gbf-put-text over gbf-put-text-clip. Passing the buffer width preserves prior behaviour exactly, because the buffer already clipped at its own edge.

author: val
body: The gx + 8 > max-x test uses 8 and not the 9-pixel pitch because a block glyph is eight pixels wide on a nine-pixel advance: gop-buf-cbf-bits writes bits 0 through 7 at x + bit. The glyph at gx therefore occupies gx through gx + 7 and fits when gx + 8 is within the edge. Testing against the pitch would drop a glyph that fits.

author: val
body: The bound here has to be an x coordinate rather than a character count, because this font advances by the per-glyph adv-table and a count cannot say where the nth glyph lands. The fit test uses gw and not adv: the cell drawn is gw wide whatever the advance is, so gw is what decides whether the glyph fits.

author: val
body: Calls to-unicode once per character, which allocates about a kilobyte per call on a path with no collector. READ on 2026-07-28 and not measured. Also still unbounded: it advances x + i * 10 against no edge, as does gop-buf-text-scaled-loop at x + i * 9 * scale. Neither is reached by the widget renderers, which is the only reason they were not bounded with the rest.
